correspondence.component_scope: Western opening into Bull Valley
correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening occupies a low feeder/ravine setting that descends east and southeast onto the Bull Valley floor, then bends northeast beside the Horseshoe Bend setting. The headward detail exposes the relief and the shared receiving floor; the selected beginning is retained without extension to another headwater.
correspondence.scope_limit: Bull Valley and Horseshoe Bend are geographic setting labels, not river-name assignments. Nearby Clover Creek is separate context and is not claimed as the selected headwater.

correspondence.component_scope: Sheep Spring Draw and the state-line approach
correspondence.finding: The northeastern valley continuation passes the directly mapped Sheep Spring Draw setting and approaches the Nevada–Utah state line. Side ravines enter the same open floor, which narrows toward Devils Gap.
correspondence.scope_limit: Sheep Spring Draw is a bounded draw/landform observation; its label is not extended upstream or across the whole composite. No additional selected tributary fragment exists.

correspondence.component_scope: Devils Gap and the northeastern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes the mapped Devils Gap road/rail corridor and continues northeast along the low valley between the western upland and the Mount Escalante/Haystack Mountain side. The contours and relief expose a continuous lower passage into the Modena outlet plain.
correspondence.scope_limit: Road and rail lines are orientation references; the selected waterway is not equated with transport infrastructure or a precise current channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Gold Springs Wash receiving outlet and Modena fan
correspondence.finding: The northwestern Gold Springs Wash exits its confined valley and bends east across the Modena setting. The selected route reaches that receiving wash near its road/rail crossing, follows the short labeled outlet/fan reach and then continues east across the low open plain beside Gray Knoll before turning northeast.
correspondence.scope_limit: Gold Springs Wash is directly read as a bounded wash label. Its northern source branch is contextual and is not added to the selected geometry; the name is not extended to all downstream basin-floor parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern cultivated receiving plain
correspondence.finding: The selected course continues northeast and east over the broad gently declining basin floor, with fields, road grids, shallow washes and isolated water features. Overlapping map coverage shows a continuous common receiving plain without a separating mountain divide. Tule Creek is mapped farther northwest, and Escalante Mine Canal farther south; neither label is borrowed for this selected interval.
correspondence.scope_limit: Ordinary connected alluvial/basin-floor geography is established; a currently wetted line through every field or dry patch is neither required nor asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Small dry basin and eastward floor continuation
correspondence.finding: The floor bends east across a small mapped dry-lake depression, then southeast and back northeast within the same low plain. The western/northern mountain front and the cultivated southern floor bound the broader receiving setting; no separate basin crossing is exposed along these selected parts.
correspondence.scope_limit: The small depression has no supported proper name in the read maps. The cartography does not prove seasonal surface-water interchange or exact wet-thread alignment.

correspondence.component_scope: Table Butte western dry-lake setting
correspondence.finding: The northeastern course reaches the mapped dry-lake depression immediately west of Table Butte and skirts its western/northern margin before continuing northeast. The depression, adjacent lowland and northward exit setting lie on the same broad continuous basin floor.
correspondence.scope_limit: Table Butte is a separate landmark, not a lake or river alias. The selected generalized line is not described as a surveyed shoreline or bank.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward basin floor and terminal approach
correspondence.finding: The route continues north through an uninterrupted low floor, east of Black Reef and the western mountain-front fans, toward the larger northern dry basin. Transport lines and a shallow road grid cross the floor without creating a cartographically established separate receiving basin.
correspondence.scope_limit: A low open floor supplies ordinary geographic correspondence; current drainage works, culvert function and hydraulic operation are unverified.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored source endpoint in the northern playa
correspondence.finding: The final part runs north, crosses the rail/road setting and turns northeast into the mapped multi-lobed northern dry-lake/playa. The stored source endpoint lies inside its northeastern lobe.
correspondence.scope_limit: The supplied endorheic class is retained. The inspected maps supply no proper name for this terminal basin.

correspondence.component_scope: Separately preserved rendered endpoint
correspondence.finding: The rendered endpoint is recorded separately and falls in the same northeastern playa lobe as the stored source endpoint. The supplied source and rendered coordinates coincide; no terminal extension or geometry change is introduced.
correspondence.scope_limit: Coincident settings do not collapse the two metadata fields or establish present water extent.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern glacial opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening occupies an ice- and snow-filled mountain trough. The selected passage runs east and southeast along the same descending glacial valley, reaching the foreland bend. Neighboring ridge-separated lakes and valleys are not substituted for the selection.
correspondence.scope_limit: Ordinary connected glacial terrain is established; no glacier name, natural-source extremity or present subglacial hydraulic route is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Foreland bend into the northbound river valley
correspondence.finding: At the eastern end of the glacial trough, the continuous receiving floor turns north and northeast into an exposed pale channel. Small lateral fans meet the same valley; the corridor is visibly continuous into the forested reach.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northbound upper valley
correspondence.finding: The river winds north through a narrow forested valley between steep ridges, with sediment bars, lateral drainage mouths and locally shadowed sections. The shared valley floor provides continuous ordinary correspondence through the easternmost bend.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern turn through the middle valley
correspondence.finding: The river bends northwest past glacier-fed side valleys and fans. Broad pale gravel sections alternate with narrower wooded reaches. Patchy cloud and mountain shadow do not sever the visible receiving valley.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Braided middle receiving floor
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor continues north through a broader gravelly river floor, receiving lateral drainage from the surrounding mountains. Bars, divided channels and vegetated surfaces occupy one connected valley.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern bend and large lateral join
correspondence.finding: The selected river swings northeast around a mountain spur, then turns northwest and west. It reaches a larger braided valley where an unselected northern channel joins. The stage3 ending is a continuation into the stage2 mainstem; it is not the marine terminal.
correspondence.scope_limit: No unselected tributary name is transferred from regional prose to a precise junction.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Westbound braided river below the lateral join
correspondence.finding: The stage2 mainstem begins at the stage3 continuation and follows the wide westward gravel-and-channel corridor. Both the short stored parts and the small southerly bend lie within this connected valley.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern river to the lake-outlet junction
correspondence.finding: The river continues northwest between forested valley sides, with numerous sediment bars. Its last part reaches the short outlet from the separate western lake, where the selected tributary pathway joins the lower mainstem.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Tezwa-side opening and river continuation
correspondence.finding: The western selected opening is already in a pale winding river. It runs northwest through a wooded valley, passing side fans and bends toward the lake approach. Its stage3 endpoint is the continuation into FID9227, not a separately stored confluence or a marine ending.
correspondence.scope_limit: The plan identifies Tezwa as the river entering Kitlope Lake. The selection starts in its lower valley; no claim is made to Tezwa’s unselected headwaters.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: River approach and Kitlope Lake entry
correspondence.finding: From the stage3 continuation, the same river turns through a low alluvial approach into the southern end of the elongated lake. The river-to-lake transfer is directly visible.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Kitlope Lake passage
correspondence.finding: The selected tributary traverses the same continuous elongated lake northward. The planning prose identifies Kitlope Lake as the lower Tezwa receiving lake; its distinctive outlet-side relation to the main valley matches the photographed setting.
correspondence.scope_limit: The lake is a separately named waterbody, not a river alias; no underwater channel is asserted.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake outlet and separate tributary confluence terminal
correspondence.finding: The lake narrows at its northern end and connects directly to the main river through a short outlet. The stored source and rendered tributary endpoints coincide at that receiving junction. This is the sole stored tributary confluence terminal, distinct from the later marine endpoint.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Shared lower river below Kitlope Lake outlet
correspondence.finding: Below the selected tributary join, the river follows broad northwestern bends through forest and bars. It remains continuously connected to the estuarine approach; the plan identifies this receiving river as Kitlope.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower channel and inner-estuary approach
correspondence.finding: The river turns west and then northwest through a widening low corridor. Pale bars and vegetated islands separate channels approaching the broad coastal receiving water. A separate northeastern river reaches the same estuarine neighborhood without replacing the selected approach.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Last selected island-and-channel setting
correspondence.finding: The last two parts reach the elongated vegetated island and adjoining channels in the inner estuary. The final short stored part remains preserved as delivered; the selection is not moved outward to open water. Planning prose places the Kitlope estuary at the head of Gardner Canal.
correspondence.scope_limit: The retained sea class is an inherited endpoint classification, not a claim that both endpoint markers lie on a surveyed open-sea shoreline.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate source sea endpoint
correspondence.finding: The stored source endpoint is west-southwest of the rendered endpoint in the inner-estuary island/channel-margin setting. It belongs to the same connected lower Kitlope receiving system and is retained separately.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate rendered sea endpoint
correspondence.finding: The rendered endpoint lies slightly northeast of the source endpoint in the same inner-estuary setting at the head of Gardner Canal. Neither endpoint is conflated with the upstream lake-outlet confluence.
correspondence.scope_limit: No exact bank, tidal stage or present channel occupancy is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based within the unchanged stored fragment, not concatenated across FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern ravine and southward feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening occupies a narrow north–south low ravine between local upland ribs. Its relief and contour pattern lead south and southwest around the low eastern knoll into the larger valley. The closer headward original exposes the receiving connection rather than relying on an extension to another headwater.
correspondence.scope_limit: The opening has no supported proper hydronym. Tracks cross this terrain but are not treated as the stream, and no present wet thread or exact-bank fit is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Join with the named Duckwater Creek
correspondence.finding: A directly labeled Duckwater Creek descends from the northwest and enters the southward valley at the selected feeder junction. The selected course continues within that common receiving valley, along the west side of the local elongated knoll and then southwest into the established trunk.
correspondence.scope_limit: The unselected northwestern named source branch remains contextual; the chosen opening and stored geometry are not replaced with it.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Duckwater valley and county-line opening
correspondence.finding: Repeated Duckwater Creek labels follow the valley south between flanking hills. The valley broadens at the White Pine–Nye county-line setting and bends southeast into the more open basin floor.
correspondence.scope_limit: Map labels support the ordinary creek corridor, not current surface discharge or legal naming extent.

correspondence.component_scope: Open creek corridor approaching Duckwater
correspondence.finding: The named creek continues south through the broad valley beside the highway and shallow alluvial terrain, then reaches the northern fields and settlement approaches at Duckwater. Small side channels and washes enter the common receiving floor.
correspondence.scope_limit: Nearby roads, ponds and fields are contextual; the selected line is not asserted to follow every modern channel or drainage work.

correspondence.component_scope: Duckwater settlement and wetland entry
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes the Duckwater Reservation settlement/field setting and turns southeast into the mapped creek wetland. The named channel and wetland share a continuous low valley at the foot of the Duckwater Hills.
correspondence.scope_limit: The jurisdiction/settlement label locates the reach and is not a river alias. Current irrigation operation is unverified.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern Duckwater wetland corridor
correspondence.finding: The long selected part follows the southeastward wetland valley below Duckwater. Repeated Duckwater Creek labels, marsh symbols and enclosing relief show one continuous receiving corridor past the hills and toward the airport-side outlet.
correspondence.scope_limit: Ordinary wetland/valley correspondence does not establish a single current wet thread, discharge or engineered-flow operation.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Duckwater channel and alluvial floor
correspondence.finding: Below the wetland the directly labeled Duckwater Creek bends southeast and south across the broad Railroad Valley floor. Bull Creek runs to the east and approaches the same lower junction setting; the selected course remains on the Duckwater side through the open fan/plain.
correspondence.scope_limit: Parallel neighboring creek lines are kept distinct; Bull Creek is not treated as a Duckwater alias.

correspondence.component_scope: Bull and Currant joining setting and southern receiving creek
correspondence.finding: The lower Duckwater course reaches the converging eastern drainage setting involving Bull Creek and the Currant Creek approach, with a Kern Creek label on a farther eastern branch. The source places Currant Creek labeling in the confluence interval and Duckwater Creek labeling again on the southern continuation. The selected route continues south on the same common valley floor toward the dry basins.
correspondence.scope_limit: Currant, Bull and Kern remain separate bounded tributary/confluence observations. Overlapping local cartographic name scope is not promoted to a verified alias or a whole-feature scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern dry basin, highway crossing and low-floor transfer
correspondence.finding: The named Duckwater Creek reaches the northern Railroad Valley dry-lake complex near the US6 crossing. The selected route passes into that pan, continues south over the intervening low floor and approaches the much larger southern playa. The mapped relief, dry-basin outlines and lowland surroundings expose one continuous terminal receiving floor.
correspondence.scope_limit: A blue channel across every dry patch is not required for ordinary receiving geography. This does not prove present seasonal water exchange or exact flood routing among the pans.

correspondence.component_scope: Entry into the larger southern playa
correspondence.finding: The southward selected corridor enters the northeastern margin of the broad southern dry-lake/playa and runs southwest into its interior. The terminal basin is part of the mapped Railroad Valley lowland, with the western and eastern mountain fronts flanking the wider floor.
correspondence.scope_limit: The playa is not renamed Duckwater Creek; the map supplies no independently confirmed proper lake name for this selected terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored endorheic source endpoint
correspondence.finding: The final short part ends within the interior of the large southern Railroad Valley playa. The source endpoint is retained in its supplied endorheic setting.
correspondence.scope_limit: No exact contemporary shoreline, water level or perennial lake is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Separately preserved rendered endpoint
correspondence.finding: The supplied rendered endpoint coincides with the stored source endpoint in the same interior playa setting and is described separately. No extra terminal extension or moved endpoint is introduced.
correspondence.scope_limit: The two metadata endpoints remain separate even though their supplied coordinates coincide.

correspondence.component_scope: Short east-northeast opening from the low slopes northeast of Eagle Crags
correspondence.finding: The opening is in a mapped minor drainage between low rocky hills. The regional original shows its eastward channel and the northward receiving bend; the upper detail supplies the enclosing terrain. This is the actual chosen opening, not a substitution of a longer southern feeder. No source or river name is printed for it.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward channel through low hills to the opening of the broader fan/valley
correspondence.finding: Regional linework follows the selected northward corridor through the low-hill gaps and out into the broader plain. The upper detail confirms the enclosing terrain and the transition from confined wash to open receiving floor. Minor side washes are distinct from the chosen route. Detailed-scale channel omissions are not interpreted as a broken geographic connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest passage across the open fan and receiving floor beside Randsburg Road
correspondence.finding: The overview maps converging wash branches and a northwest continuation into the common valley floor east of the Slate Range. The detailed original shows one continuous descending open floor, with fan surfaces rather than an intervening separate basin. Ordinary correspondence is established without requiring the rendered line to coincide with a precise dry channel or every road crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward turn and constricted receiving corridor east of Slate Range
correspondence.finding: The route turns north around the eastern foot of the Slate Range and follows the continuous axial floor past lateral fans. Regional blue channel linework can be followed through this interval; upper and middle detailed topography independently locate the narrowed passage and its wider northern opening. The selected route does not cross west into Searles Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Wingate Wash joining setting and northward valley passage toward the playa
correspondence.finding: Wingate Wash is printed on the eastern side branch approaching the selected receiving corridor near the beginning of this interval. The chosen line arrives from the south, then continues northwest and north through the low gap into the broader southern Panamint floor. The overview depicts the joins and the connected axial wash; the middle detail depicts the same enclosed passage. The label on the eastern branch does not demonstrate that the entire selected upper route or downstream playa is named Wingate Wash.

correspondence.component_scope: Fan-to-playa transition and southern lobe of the elongate receiving pan
correspondence.finding: The channel and open fan enter the southern lobe of the elongate playa. Regional drainage linework and the middle/terminal cartography show an uninterrupted receiving floor as the lobe widens northward. A currently wet thread through the pan is neither needed nor asserted. The valley name is regional context, not a proper name assigned to this modeled river.

correspondence.component_scope: Long central dry-lake floor and narrowing northward passage
correspondence.finding: The selected route traverses the broad central playa and its northward narrowing, within the same continuous mapped pan. Side fans enter from the bounding ranges; there is no required separate-basin or lake-to-feeder transfer at this scale. The straight rendered interval is described as a generalized playa-floor passage, not a named natural channel or evidence of permanent water.

correspondence.component_scope: Connected northern lobes and actual selected endpoint
correspondence.finding: The terminal original shows a continuous northward series of adjoining playa lobes beneath the western foot of the Panamint Range. The selection bends northeast inside the final lobe and stops within that playa near its northeastern margin, before the separate drainage entering from the north/east. The source endpoint and rendered endpoint are retained as separate stored fields and both occupy this same terminal setting. No extension beyond the ending, named lake outlet, sea connection or whole-valley traversal is added.
